extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — grant applicants, peer reviewers, institutional research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: A news index summarizing recent NIH updates to policies, processes, formats, and resources that affect preparing, submitting, and managing NIH grant applications and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate models for research (New Approach Methodologies - NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches and encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential; investigators must choose models appropriate to their scientific question when designing studies (context: NAMs).

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects: award structure and application format
rubrics_metrics.description: "New Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure — watch NIH’s 6-minute overview to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants to PF5 should follow the specified application format and be aware that, after peer review and before Just-in-Time, applications may be split into linked awards; view NIH overview for key features and formatting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans, investigators should use the 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified required elements specified by NIH for pilot submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to embed replication and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "Embedding Replication and Reproducibility Throughout NIH Research: Key Reminders for Applications, Awards, and a New Highlighted Topic"; NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility and launched a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and awardees should consider reliability, plans for replication, and practices that enhance reproducibility in applications and project designs; NIH is prioritizing and incentivizing replication/reproducibility activities across the research enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Competitive But Not Discussed' scoring designation and its meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: "Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This designation indicates an application scored in the middle third of the study section that will not receive discussion; applicants receiving this status were judged competitive but were not discussed due to percentile/cutoff procedures implemented during emergency modifications to review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of NIH peer review within CSR
rubrics_metrics.description: "All peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) — one-year update describing consolidation and its initial effects on the peer-review process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review procedures, assignment, and administration are consolidated under CSR to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency; applicants and reviewers should expect procedural/administrative impacts from centralization (e.g., study section management, review workflows).
